title: Evening Brief — Sun 22 Nov

stories.board: World climate talks end with no deal
stories.headline: COP31 climate meeting in Turkey falls apart
stories.what: After two weeks plus two extra days, countries rejected the final plan on Sunday. The fight was over whether to name fossil fuels (oil, coal and gas). It is the first time since 2009 that these UN talks ended with no shared deal.
stories.why: These meetings are how the world agrees on ways to slow global warming.
stories.sides: The EU, Panama and small island nations refused a plan that skips fossil fuels; Saudi Arabia and Russia backed leaving them out. UN chief Guterres called it deeply disappointing.

sources.name: ABC News (Australia), with Reuters and AP

stories.board: Netanyahu and Eisenkot talk 4 hours, no deal
stories.headline: Israel unity talks end without a deal, more talks planned
stories.what: Likud and Eisenkot's Yashar party met for over four hours in Herzliya but did not agree. They plan to meet again, maybe Monday.
stories.why: The result decides who leads Israel's next government.
stories.sides: Both still want to be prime minister first; they also split on Ben-Gvir joining and on who picks the October 7 inquiry (official investigation) team.

stories.board: Ottawa keeps fighting Stellantis Brampton plant sale
stories.headline: Canada and Ontario push Stellantis on Brampton car plant
stories.what: Stellantis wants to sell its closed Brampton car plant to Roshel, an armoured vehicle maker. Friday's meeting with Ottawa, Ontario and the union ended with only more talks planned.
stories.why: About 2,000 laid-off workers and at least 222 million dollars of public money are at stake.
stories.sides: No major disagreement between parties: Carney called the sale a betrayal, and Ontario and the Unifor union are pushing back with Ottawa; Stellantis says nothing has changed.

quick_hits: Flu is rising in Canada: 14.5 percent of flu tests came back positive in the week to Nov. 14.
PM Carney brought a Trump impersonator (actor who copies him) on stage to joke at Ottawa's press dinner.
Ottawa gave Stellantis until about Dec. 12 to pay back subsidy (government help) money or face legal action.
big_picture: A day of stuck talks: the world on climate, Israel on its next government, and Canada on its car jobs.
